```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ── Prerequisites (run once) ───────────────────────────────────────────
#   if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
#       install.packages("BiocManager")
#   BiocManager::install("curatedMetagenomicData")
#   install.packages(c("kableExtra", "ggplot2", "patchwork"))

library(curatedMetagenomicData)
library(kableExtra)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, cache=TRUE, cache.lazy=FALSE)

pretty_table <- function(df, caption="", digits=2, max.rows=NULL) {
    if (!is.null(max.rows) && nrow(df) > max.rows) {
        df <- head(df, max.rows)
        caption <- paste0(caption, " (showing first ", max.rows, " rows)")
    }
    df %>%
        kbl(caption=caption, digits=digits, booktabs=TRUE) %>%
        kable_styling(bootstrap_options=c("striped","hover","condensed"),
                      full_width=FALSE, font_size=11) %>%
        scroll_box(width="100%", height="400px")
}
```

# 1.  Resolve one disease label per subject

```{r subject-resolve, cache=TRUE}
# ── Problem ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1. Many subjects are sampled multiple times (repeated measures).
# 2. Some subjects have inconsistent disease labels across their samples
#    (e.g. subject TettAJ_20164: 3×"arthritis;psoriasis" + 1×"arthritis").
# 3. Sample-level counting inflates comorbidity numbers.
#
# → Solution: aggregate to one majority-vote label per subject.

sm <- sampleMetadata

# Split disease into individual conditions
sm$disease_list <- strsplit(sm$disease, ";")

# Per subject: collect all samples, take most frequent disease label
subject_samples <- split(sm, sm$subject_id)

resolve_subject_disease <- function(df) {
    all_combos <- table(df$disease)
    # If all samples say "healthy", keep healthy
    # Otherwise, pick the most frequent non-empty disease label
    names(sort(all_combos, decreasing=TRUE))[1]
}

subj_ids <- names(subject_samples)
subj_disease <- unname(vapply(subject_samples, resolve_subject_disease, character(1)))

cat("Total subjects in curatedMetagenomicData:",
    length(subj_disease), "\n")
cat("Unique disease labels (after resolution):",
    length(unique(subj_disease)), "\n\n")

# ── Also: how many subjects had inconsistent labels? ──────────────────
inconsistent_count <- sum(sapply(subject_samples,
    function(s) length(unique(s$disease)) > 1))
cat("Subjects with inconsistent samples:", inconsistent_count, "\n")

# ── Build subject-centric metadata ─────────────────────────────────────
subj_meta <- data.frame(
    subject_id = subj_ids,
    disease    = subj_disease,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Add columns from first sample occurrence (fast)
sm_first <- sm[match(subj_ids, sm$subject_id), ]
subj_meta$study_name <- sm_first$study_name
subj_meta$body_site  <- sm_first$body_site
subj_meta$gender     <- sm_first$gender
subj_meta$age        <- sm_first$age
subj_meta$country    <- sm_first$country
subj_meta$n_samples  <- as.integer(unname(sapply(subject_samples, nrow)))
```

# 2.  Subject-level comorbidity search

```{r comorbidity-search, cache=TRUE}
# Split resolved diseases into individual conditions
condition_list <- strsplit(subj_meta$disease, ";")
all_conditions <- sort(unique(unlist(condition_list)))
all_conditions <- setdiff(all_conditions, "healthy")

# Binary matrix: subjects × conditions
cond_mat <- vapply(all_conditions, function(c) {
    grepl(c, subj_meta$disease, fixed=TRUE)
}, logical(nrow(subj_meta)))

cat("Unique disease conditions (excl. healthy):", length(all_conditions), "\n")

# Count every pair
pairs <- list()
for (i in seq_along(all_conditions)) {
    for (j in seq_len(i - 1L)) {
        da <- all_conditions[i]; db <- all_conditions[j]
        na  <- sum( cond_mat[,i] &  !cond_mat[,j])
        nb  <- sum(!cond_mat[,i] &   cond_mat[,j])
        nab <- sum( cond_mat[,i] &   cond_mat[,j])
        if (nab >= 1) {
            pairs[[length(pairs) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
                Disease_A = da, Disease_B = db,
                A_only = na, B_only = nb, Both = nab,
                Total = na + nb + nab,
                Prop_both = round(nab / (na + nb + nab), 3)
            )
        }
    }
}
comorb <- do.call(rbind, pairs)
comorb <- comorb[order(comorb$Both, decreasing=TRUE), ]
rownames(comorb) <- NULL

cat("Disease pairs with non-zero comorbidity:", nrow(comorb), "\n")
```

```{r comorb-table, results="asis"}
comorb %>%
    pretty_table(caption=paste0("All ", nrow(comorb),
        " disease pairs with ≥1 comorbid subject"),
        max.rows=35)
```

## 2.1  Skin-relevant pairs

```{r skin-pairs}
skin_terms <- c("psoriasis","arthritis","AD","AR","asthma",
                "acne","eczema","dermatitis","rosacea")
skin_mask <- grepl(paste(skin_terms,collapse="|"),
                   comorb$Disease_A, ignore.case=TRUE) |
             grepl(paste(skin_terms,collapse="|"),
                   comorb$Disease_B, ignore.case=TRUE)
skin_comorb <- comorb[skin_mask, ]

skin_comorb %>%
    pretty_table(caption=paste0("Skin-relevant pairs (n=", nrow(skin_comorb), ")"))
```

> **⚠️ `AD` is ambiguous across studies**: In ChngKR_2016 (skin), `AD` =
> Atopic Dermatitis. In all other studies, `AD` = Alzheimer's Disease.
> Results here pool both. See Section 4 for disambiguation.

# 4.  Skin studies — subject-level deep dive

## 4.1  Which studies contain skin samples?

```{r skin-studies}
skin_idx <- which(subj_meta$body_site == "skin")
cat("Subjects with skin samples:", length(skin_idx), "\n\n")

skin_study_tab <- as.data.frame(table(Study = subj_meta$study_name[skin_idx]))
colnames(skin_study_tab) <- c("Study", "Subjects")
skin_study_tab %>%
    kbl(caption="Skin studies — subject counts", booktabs=TRUE) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options=c("striped","condensed"), full_width=FALSE)

# Disease distribution per skin study
for (study in unique(subj_meta$study_name[skin_idx])) {
    sidx <- which(subj_meta$study_name == study & subj_meta$body_site == "skin")
    tab <- as.data.frame(table(Disease = subj_meta$disease[sidx]))
    colnames(tab) <- c("Disease", "Subjects")
    cat("\n**", study, "** — ", length(sidx), " subjects\n\n", sep="")
    print(kbl(tab, booktabs=TRUE) %>%
          kable_styling(bootstrap_options=c("striped","condensed"), full_width=FALSE))
}
```

## 4.2  TettAJ_2016 — Psoriasis cohort

```{r tett-subjects, cache=TRUE}
tett_orig <- as.data.frame(colData(
    curatedMetagenomicData("TettAJ_2016.relative_abundance",

cat("── RAW samples:", ncol(tett_orig), "──\n")
```

## 4.4  `AD` disambiguation: Atopic Dermatitis vs Alzheimer's Disease

```{r ad-disambig}
ad_studies <- which(grepl("\\bAD\\b", subj_meta$disease))
cat("Studies where 'AD' appears as a disease label:\n\n")
for (study in unique(subj_meta$study_name[ad_studies])) {
    sidx <- which(subj_meta$study_name == study & grepl("\\bAD\\b", subj_meta$disease))
    n  <- length(sidx)
    bs <- paste(unique(subj_meta$body_site[sidx]), collapse=",")
    cat(sprintf("  %-35s body_site=%-15s n_subj=%d\n", study, bs, n))
}

cat("\n\n➡ Only ChngKR_2016 uses 'AD' as **Atopic Dermatitis** (skin site).\n")
cat("➡ All other studies use 'AD' as **Alzheimer's Disease**.\n")
cat("➡ When modelling, restrict to body_site == 'skin' to avoid ambiguity.\n")
```

# 5.  Download and average abundance per subject

```{r download, cache=TRUE}
# ── Download species-level MetaPhlAn3 abundance ────────────────────────
tett_se <- curatedMetagenomicData("TettAJ_2016.relative_abundance",
                                   dryrun=FALSE, counts=FALSE)[[1]]
chng_se <- curatedMetagenomicData("ChngKR_2016.relative_abundance",
                                   dryrun=FALSE, counts=FALSE)[[1]]
ohj_se  <- curatedMetagenomicData("OhJ_2014.relative_abundance",
                                   dryrun=FALSE, counts=FALSE)[[1]]

cat("Dimensions (taxa × samples):\n")
cat("  TettAJ_2016:", nrow(tett_se), "×", ncol(tett_se), "\n")
cat("  ChngKR_2016:", nrow(chng_se), "×", ncol(chng_se), "\n")
cat("  OhJ_2014:   ", nrow(ohj_se),  "×", ncol(ohj_se),  "\n\n")

# ── Average abundance per subject (handle repeated measures) ───────────
# For each study: group columns by subject_id, average abundance

average_by_subject <- function(se) {
    abund <- assay(se)
    meta  <- as.data.frame(colData(se))
    subjects <- unique(meta$subject_id)
    result_list <- list()
    for (s in subjects) {
        sidx <- which(meta$subject_id == s)
        if (length(sidx) == 1) {
            result_list[[s]] <- abund[, sidx]
        } else {
            result_list[[s]] <- rowMeans(abund[, sidx])
        }
    }
    do.call(cbind, result_list)
}

tett_avg <- average_by_subject(tett_se)
chng_avg <- average_by_subject(chng_se)
ohj_avg  <- average_by_subject(ohj_se)

cat("Subject-averaged dimensions (taxa × subjects):\n")
cat("  TettAJ_2016:", nrow(tett_avg), "×", ncol(tett_avg), "\n")
cat("  ChngKR_2016:", nrow(chng_avg), "×", ncol(chng_avg), "\n")
cat("  OhJ_2014:   ", nrow(ohj_avg),  "×", ncol(ohj_avg),  "\n")
```

## 5.1  Common taxa across studies

```{r common-taxa}
common <- Reduce(intersect, list(
    rownames(tett_avg), rownames(chng_avg), rownames(ohj_avg)))
cat("Taxa present in all three studies: **", length(common), "**\n\n")

# Top shared taxa
means <- sort(rowMeans(tett_avg[common, ]), decreasing=TRUE)
data.frame(
    Taxon = names(head(means, 10)),
    `Mean %` = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * head(means, 10))) %>%
    kbl(caption="Top 10 shared taxa by abundance (TettAJ_2016, subject-averaged)",
        booktabs=TRUE) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options=c("striped","condensed"), full_width=FALSE)
```

## 5.2  Build merged subject-level dataset

```{r merge}
merged_abund <- cbind(
    tett_avg[common, ],
    chng_avg[common, ],
    ohj_avg[common, ]
)

# Subject-level metadata for merged dataset
tett_subj_meta <- unique(as.data.frame(colData(tett_se))[, c("subject_id","disease")])
chng_subj_meta <- unique(as.data.frame(colData(chng_se))[, c("subject_id","disease")])

# Resolve per-subject disease consistently
resolve_dis <- function(vec) names(sort(table(vec), decreasing=TRUE))[1]

meta <- rbind(
    data.frame(study="TettAJ_2016",
               subject_id = colnames(tett_avg),
               disease = sapply(split(tett_subj_meta$disease, tett_subj_meta$subject_id), resolve_dis)),
    data.frame(study="ChngKR_2016",
               subject_id = colnames(chng_avg),
               disease = sapply(split(chng_subj_meta$disease, chng_subj_meta$subject_id), resolve_dis)),
    data.frame(study="OhJ_2014",
               subject_id = colnames(ohj_avg),
               disease = "healthy")
)

# Multi-label encoding
meta$pso  <- grepl("psoriasis", meta$disease, ignore.case=TRUE)
meta$ad   <- grepl("^AD",       meta$disease)
meta$ar   <- grepl("^AR",       meta$disease)
meta$arth <- grepl("^arthritis",meta$disease)
meta$healthy <- meta$disease == "healthy"

cat("Merged dataset: ", nrow(merged_abund), " taxa × ",
    ncol(merged_abund), " subjects\n")
```

# 6.  Feasibility assessment

```{r feasibility}
feas <- data.frame(
    Pair = c(
        "Psoriasis vs Psoriasis+Arthritis (Tett)",
        "AD only vs AD+AR (Chng)",
        "AD only vs AD+Asthma (Chng)",
        "Cross-study: Psoriasis ←→ AD",
        "Synthetic Psoriasis+AD mix"
    ),
    Design = c("2-group","2-group","2-group (AR confound)","cross-generalisation","simulation"),
    N_A = c("21","5","5","28 (Tett)","—"),
    N_Both = c("7","8","2 AD;asthma + 4 AD;AR;asthma","0","—"),
    N_B_only = c("—","1 (excluded)","0","39 (Chng)","—"),
    N_healthy = c("47 (OhJ+HMP)","15","15","62","47"),
    Viability = c(
        "✅ Viable. Test: does arthritis alter psoriasis signature? Consider age matching (Tett is older).",
        "✅ Best skin option. N small (5 vs 8) — bootstrap or Bayesian approach. Exclude AR-only (n=1).",
        "❌ No pure asthma group. AD;asthma (n=2) + AD;AR;asthma (n=4) — AR confounds interpretation.",
        "⚠️  Tests whether disease-specific markers generalise across diseases/studies. No real comorbidity.",
        "✅ Method development: mix real profiles at known proportions, validate recovery of mixing weights.")) %>%
    kbl(caption="Feasibility of multi-label disentanglement designs (subject level)",
        booktabs=TRUE) %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options=c("striped","condensed"), full_width=FALSE) %>%
    column_spec(7, width="28em")
```

> **Why subject-level matters:** TettAJ_2016 has 89 samples but only 28 subjects.
> Averaging per subject removes the pseudo-replication that would inflate
> statistical significance. We lose sample size but gain honest inference.

# 7.  Beyond skin: positive controls with larger comorbid groups

```{r positive-controls}
other <- comorb[
    !grepl(paste(skin_terms,collapse="|"), comorb$Disease_A, ignore.case=TRUE) &
    !grepl(paste(skin_terms,collapse="|"), comorb$Disease_B, ignore.case=TRUE) &
    comorb$A_only >= 20 & comorb$B_only >= 20 & comorb$Both >= 20, ]
other %>%
    pretty_table(caption=paste0("Non-skin pairs with ≥20 subjects in all groups (n=",
                 nrow(other), ") — ideal for method validation"))
```

# 9.  Data quality notes

| Issue | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **TettAJ_2016 repeated measures** | 89 samples from 28 subjects (2–4 per subject). Averaged per subject in Section 5. |
| **TettAJ_20164 mislabel** | 3 of 4 samples say `arthritis;psoriasis`, 1 says `arthritis`. Likely data entry error. Resolved by majority vote to `arthritis;psoriasis`. |
| **AD ambiguity** | `AD` = Alzheimer's Disease in 6 studies (stool), but **Atopic Dermatitis** in ChngKR_2016 (skin). Filter by `body_site == "skin"` to isolate Atopic Dermatitis. |
| **ChngKR_2016 country mix** | Subjects from Singapore, China, Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei. Potential population structure. FLG genotype available. |
| **Age mismatch** | Tett (32–80 yrs) vs OhJ healthy (20–40 yrs). Age may confound disease signature. |
| **Sequencing + extraction** | Tett: Illumina HiSeq + MoBio. Chng: Illumina HiSeq + Qiagen. Batch effects possible. |
